title: Harden queue consumers for adaptive backpressure and poison-message handling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor and harden our queue consumer stack (Redis workers + Kafka consumers) to reduce transient failures, control retry storms, and provide robust poison-message handling. Current issues: consumers sometimes overload downstream services under bursty load, retry logic causes thundering retry storms after infra flaps, and there is inconsistent DLQ behavior across queue types. This ticket will standardize retry semantics, introduce an adaptive concurrency/backpressure mechanism at the consumer level, and add deterministic DLQ paths for both Redis and Kafka workloads. We also plan to upgrade key client deps (go-redis and sarama/confluent clients) as part of the work to pick up bugfixes and better instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Consumers expose an adaptive concurrency limit (configurable) that prevents downstream saturation and is validated by load tests
Retry semantics are uniform: bounded retry budget, exponential backoff with jitter, and idempotency keys to prevent duplication
Poison messages are reliably routed to per-topic/queue DLQs with an SLA for observability (metric + alert)
Dependency upgrades applied: go-redis >= v10 and sarama >= 1.43 (or equivalent), with migration notes in the PR
No regression in end-to-end latency for steady-state traffic (<= 5% increase); throughput loss under saturation is acceptable if it prevents downstream failures
Integration tests cover Redis stream consumer, Redis list worker, and Kafka consumer paths including DLQ routing
plan: Audit existing consumer implementations to enumerate current retry/backoff logic and identify differences between Redis and Kafka paths
Design: document adaptive concurrency model (token-bucket + slow-start) and how consumers signal backpressure to router layer
Implement a small consumer library shim with: acquire/process/release lifecycle, retry-budget enforcement, idempotency hook, and DLQ writer
Upgrade go-redis and Kafka client libraries in a feature branch, fix breaking API changes, and add needed metrics
Run staged load tests in staging (burst + recovery scenarios) to tune default configs
Roll out as a canary to <10% of workers, monitor errors/latency, then ramp to 100% with automatic rollback on regressions
Document migration steps and update runbooks and dashboards (DLQ counts, retry budget exhaustion, consumer concurrency)
decisions: Keep broker-level features (Kafka consumer pause/unpause, Redis XGROUP) as fallbacks but implement primary backpressure at the consumer shim for consistent cross-queue behavior
Use application-level retry budget instead of unlimited broker redelivery to avoid retry storms after transient infra issues
Implement DLQs per logical queue/topic instead of a global DLQ to make root-cause debugging easier
Upgrade client libraries proactively to pick up instrumentation and bugfixes; perform compatibility tests before rolling to production
